# dsh-context-reclaim
**Tool results are reclaimed before they enter history, so the prompt cache never goes cold.**
> ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up upd
**DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates.
> 🟢 **Collision risk: very low.** It occupies **5 server-side seams and 0 client slots** — measured
alongside the **19 same-track plugins** among the 44 installed here, with no conflict, and it takes
**no `chain` slot** (the only kind that makes plugins displace each other). See Compatibility.
**English** · 简体中文
## What this is
A DSH session's context is not blown up by the conversation; it is blown up by **tool results**: a s
ingle `read` of several hundred lines, a single `pwsh` dumping a wall of logs, a system prompt repea
ted verbatim every turn. Once this content has entered the history, the only thing left is for the c
ompactor to operate on it after the fact — and compaction has to rewrite already-committed history,
which knocks out the whole server-side prefix cache and makes every compaction more expensive than t
ocks out the whole server-side prefix cache and makes every compaction more expensive than the last.
`dsh-context-reclaim` moves to a different position: it handles them **before the tool result is app
ended to history**, and it never rewrites content that has already been committed. So the prefix cac
he is never invalidated because of this plugin.
It hooks into 5 seams:
| Seam | What it does | Default |
| `tools/post-execute` | Purify a tool result the moment it is produced + bound it by content type,

inserting a retrieval pointer at the truncation point | on |
| `system-prompt/assemble` | Fold the t
ool definition surface, stabilize the order of prefix sections, truncate over-long description lines

| on |
| `tools/pre-execute` | Duplicate-edit interception (a second identical edit to the same con

tent of the same file is rejected outright) | on |
| `session/event` | Compaction-summary integrity

audit (warns when a compaction summary is missing sections) | on |
| `llm/stream` | One cost-attribu
tion line per request, printing route / prompt / cache hit / output | on |
## 1. Tool-result purification and bounding
This is the core. Every time a tool call returns, the plugin first performs **lossless purification*
*, then **bounding**.
### Lossless purification
Collapses ANSI escape sequences, strips trailing whitespace, normalizes CR. This step is pure purifi
cation and loses no information.
It only acts when the content meets **both** thresholds: length ≥ 32 characters, and a reduction rat
io after purification ≥ 0.2%. Small results are not touched at all.
Turn it off: `config.noise = false`, or the environment variable `DSH_RECLAIM_NOISE=0`.
### Bounding by content type
Different types of tool results have completely different tolerances. The plugin sorts tools into th
pes of tool results have completely different tolerances. The plugin sorts tools into three classes:
| Class | Tools covered | Head / tail kept | Per-line cap | Total character cap |
[该节后续省略]
### The other official patches: what a plugin can and cannot replace
Stated plainly, because installing these plugins does **not** make the other file patches unnecessar
ated plainly, because installing these plugins does **not** make the other file patches unnecessary:
| Official 1.5 file patch | Edits | Can a plugin replace it? |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` — writable request | `lib/index.js` | ✅ **Yes — done by this plugin, see ab

ove** |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar` — `flex-wrap` on the footer slot | `lib/lib-client.js

` | ✅ Yes (a client plugin can inject CSS); not shipped here |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop` — run
time-snapshot reclaim, system-prompt convergence | `lib/index.js` | ❌ No — needs the loop's private

projection class and its commit point |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` — `splitSystemPrompt` collect
s every leading system message | `lib/index.js` | ❌ No, and it is pointless without the `dsh-agent-l

oop` patch |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner` — result pruning + load-bearing guar
d | `lib/index.js` | ❌ No — the host instantiates the exported class directly; there is no registrat

ion seam |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer` — `conversation.chat.turnTail` chain election | `

lib/client.js` | ❌ No — the official client bundle itself must be edited |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sessi
on-format-v1-to-v2` — `turn/start` repair | `lib/index.js` | ❌ No — runs inside the session restore

path |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` — the same, persistence side | `lib/worker.cjs

` | ❌ No — runs in a worker thread |
| `@earendil-works/pi-ai` — `max_tokens` floor | `dist/api/simp
le-options.js` | ❌ No — third-party dist, its ESM namespace is read-only |
In short: the one patch that these plugins *had* to depend on is gone. The rest are independent impr
ovements that change how DSH's own machinery behaves, and they remain optional. To apply any of them
, use the patch library: <https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-patch-library>.
## Compatibility
### 🔗 With `dsh-capability-composer`
reclaim internally maintains an ownership table of "which section of the system prompt belongs to wh
om" (`SECTION_OWNER`), in which the "available plugins" section belongs to `dsh-capability-composer`
m" (`SECTION_OWNER`), in which the "available plugins" section belongs to `dsh-capability-composer`.
In other words: **the plugin list should not be trimmed by reclaim** — that is the capability compos
er's job. When both are installed, narrowing of the section is carried out by the composer, and recl
aim only keeps the default behaviour when the composer is absent.
